pageContent: Srinagar ranks among Jammu and Kashmir's most rewarding destinations, and it is easy to see why travelers keep returning. Known for city of lakes, mughal gardens, and timeless kashmir craftsmanship, it packs a remarkable variety of experiences into one trip. When people search for the best places to visit in Srinagar, the headline names come up again and again: Dal Lake, Shikara Ride on Dal Lake, Shalimar Bagh, Nishat Bagh, Chashme Shahi. Each earns its spot for a reason — together they capture the city, heritage, lake character that defines the region.

Beyond the icons, the must visit places in Srinagar reward anyone willing to explore a little further. Spots such as Hazratbal Shrine, Jama Masjid Srinagar, Shankaracharya Temple, Dal Lake Houseboat Stay, Lal Chowk round out an itinerary and show a different side of the destination. For the best experience, time your visit thoughtfully: many of the top tourist attractions in Srinagar are at their finest early in the day or around golden hour, when the light is soft, crowds are thin, and photographs come alive. Most travelers find that two to four unhurried days are enough to cover the essentials without rushing.

Looking for things to do in Srinagar that go beyond the guidebook? Group the Dal Lake and Shikara Ride on Dal Lake area together to cut travel time, and keep a relaxed half-day spare for the hidden gems and spontaneous detours that make city and heritage and lake so memorable. attractions.name: Dal Lake
attractions.description: The soul of Srinagar, Dal Lake stretches 18 sq km across the eastern edge of the city, framed by the Zabarwan hills and the Pir Panjal range. It is home to an extraordinary floating city — shikaras, houseboats, floating gardens (rad), vegetable markets on water, and schools on boats — all functioning as they have for centuries. Dawn on the lake when mist drifts across the lotus beds is among the most evocative travel experiences in Asia.
attractions.whyVisit: No visit to Kashmir is complete without experiencing the unique floating world of Dal Lake at sunrise.
attractions.bestTime: April to October for general; December to February for the dramatic snow-frosted scenery
attractions.duration: Half day to full day; overnight on houseboat

attractions.name: Shikara Ride on Dal Lake
attractions.description: The quintessential Kashmir experience, a shikara ride glides silently past lotus beds, vegetable gardens, duck farms, and moored houseboats. Morning rides catch the floating vegetable and flower market that assembles before dawn in the centre of the lake. Evening rides are lit by golden reflections of the Zabarwan hills. Shikara wallahs typically carry a small carved wooden trunk selling saffron, papier-mache, and carved wood souvenirs.
attractions.whyVisit: Float through the floating vegetable market and lotus gardens at dawn — the most iconic Kashmir moment.
attractions.bestTime: Early morning for the flower market; evening for reflections

attractions.name: Shalimar Bagh
attractions.description: Built by Mughal Emperor Jahangir for his wife Nur Jahan in 1619, Shalimar Bagh is the grandest of Srinagar's three Mughal gardens. It is laid out across four terraces with a central canal fed by a mountain stream, flanked by double rows of ancient chinar trees. The uppermost zenana garden with its black marble pavilion and cascading fountains remains one of the finest expressions of Mughal landscape art in the subcontinent.
attractions.whyVisit: The crown jewel of Mughal garden design — 400 years old and still astonishing in its symmetry and scale.
attractions.bestTime: March to April for chinar bloom; October for autumn colours

attractions.name: Nishat Bagh
attractions.description: The 'Garden of Bliss', built in 1633 by Asif Khan, brother of Nur Jahan, Nishat Bagh is terraced in twelve levels representing the twelve signs of the zodiac. Its central water channel descends the entire height of the garden in cascades and fountains, terminating at Dal Lake. Ancient chinar trees, some over 400 years old and with 20 m trunk circumferences, line every terrace.
attractions.whyVisit: The largest and most layered of the Srinagar Mughal gardens, with 400-year-old chinar trees of extraordinary size.
attractions.bestTime: March to May; October for autumn chinar

attractions.name: Chashme Shahi
attractions.description: The smallest of the three Mughal gardens, Chashme Shahi ('Royal Spring') was built by Shah Jahan in 1632 around a natural freshwater spring considered sacred and reputedly medicinal. Compact but finely proportioned, its terraced design frames a view of Dal Lake below between rows of cypress and flowering beds. Local residents still fill bottles from the spring, which flows clean year-round.
attractions.whyVisit: A perfectly scaled Mughal garden built around a natural medicinal spring with commanding Dal Lake views.

attractions.name: Hazratbal Shrine
attractions.description: Srinagar's most sacred Islamic site, Hazratbal ('Majestic Place') stands on the western shore of Dal Lake and enshrines the Moi-e-Muqqadas — a hair of the Prophet Muhammad, brought to Kashmir in 1700. The gleaming white marble domed mosque, built in 1979, is the only domed mosque in Kashmir and draws enormous crowds on Fridays and Islamic holy days.
attractions.whyVisit: Kashmir's holiest mosque, housing a relic of the Prophet Muhammad — serene on weekdays, electrifying on holy days.

attractions.name: Jama Masjid Srinagar
attractions.description: Built in 1402 by Sultan Sikandar and repeatedly rebuilt after fires, Srinagar's Jama Masjid is the largest mosque in Kashmir and an iconic example of Indo-Saracenic architecture. Its 378 wooden pillars, each made from a single deodar cedar trunk, support a vast courtyard that can hold 33,000 worshippers. The four tapering minarets are a defining feature of the Srinagar skyline.
attractions.whyVisit: The most architecturally significant mosque in Kashmir — 378 individual deodar cedar columns under one vast courtyard.
attractions.bestTime: Friday for prayers; early morning for solitude

attractions.name: Shankaracharya Temple
attractions.description: Perched on a 1,000-step climb atop Shankaracharya Hill at 1,000 m above the Dal Lake basin, this ancient Shiva temple is the oldest in Srinagar, its core dating to the 9th century. The view from the hilltop at dawn — Dal Lake shimmering below, Shalimar Bagh visible, and the full Pir Panjal range behind — is the finest panoramic perspective of the city available.
attractions.whyVisit: Srinagar's oldest temple on its highest hill — the finest single panoramic viewpoint over the city and Dal Lake.
attractions.bestTime: Sunrise for the view; April to October for climbing

attractions.name: Dal Lake Houseboat Stay
attractions.description: Srinagar's wooden houseboats — developed during British rule when foreigners could not own land in Kashmir — are floating palaces of carved walnut and cedar panelling, Persian-style carpets, and silver-topped kangri firepots. Over 1,000 licensed houseboats are moored on Dal and Nagin Lakes, ranging from basic lodgings to luxury suites. Waking to the sound of oars and the call to prayer across the water is unforgettable.
attractions.whyVisit: Sleep on a century-old carved cedar houseboat moored on Dal Lake — a uniquely Kashmiri luxury.
attractions.bestTime: April to October; December for winter houseboat experience

attractions.name: Lal Chowk
attractions.description: The historic heart of Srinagar's commercial life, Lal Chowk has been the city's main square and political focal point for over a century. The clock tower and surrounding multi-storey shopfronts are draped in colourful fabric and Kashmir goods. The lanes radiating outward lead to the old city's craft bazaars — silverwork, papier-mache, walnut carving, and the carpet workshops of the Bohri Kadal area.
attractions.whyVisit: Srinagar's beating commercial heart — the gateway to the old city's labyrinthine craft bazaars.
attractions.bestTime: Morning for shopping; evening for street food

attractions.name: Old City Srinagar (Shehr-e-Khaas)
attractions.description: The old city — locally called Shehr-e-Khaas — between Jama Masjid and the Jhelum River is a dense medieval streetscape of timber-framed houses with latticed windows, neighbourhood mosques, and artisan workshops. The craft quarters are organised by trade: booksellers, bakers, copperworkers, and weavers each occupy distinct lanes unchanged in function if not in structure for centuries.
attractions.whyVisit: Walk the medieval streetscape of a living Kashmiri city where artisan traditions have continued for 500 years.

attractions.name: Nagin Lake
attractions.description: Separated from Dal Lake by a narrow embankment, Nagin ('Jewel in the Ring') is the smaller and cleaner of Srinagar's two great lakes. It hosts fewer houseboats and is significantly quieter, giving a more intimate version of the Dal Lake experience. The surrounding willow-lined shores and the reflected image of Zabarwan hills in its clear water make it especially beautiful at dawn.
attractions.whyVisit: Dal Lake's quieter, cleaner twin — the same houseboat and shikara experience without the crowds.

attractions.name: Char Chinar (Roza Bal Island)
attractions.description: A small island at the southern end of Dal Lake, Char Chinar — 'Four Chinars' — is named for the four ancient plane trees planted at its corners. The island is accessible only by shikara and appears on millions of Kashmir photographs: a perfect circle of chinar flame reflected in still water. The four trees are believed to be over 400 years old.
attractions.whyVisit: The most iconic island image in Kashmir — four ancient chinar trees rising from the centre of Dal Lake.
attractions.bestTime: October for autumn red; April to May for fresh green

attractions.name: Shah Hamadan Shrine (Khanqah-e-Moula)
attractions.description: The most beautiful mosque in Srinagar, Khanqah-e-Moula stands on the west bank of the Jhelum River and was built in 1395 in honour of Mir Syed Ali Hamadani, who brought Islam to Kashmir. The tall octagonal structure is entirely of wood — papier-mache walls, carved eaves, painted floral ceilings — and is one of the finest examples of Central Asian wooden architecture in South Asia. Non-Muslims may not enter the inner sanctum.
attractions.whyVisit: The most exquisite wooden mosque in South Asia — a masterpiece of Central Asian architecture on the Jhelum bank.
attractions.bestTime: Morning for soft light on the façade

attractions.name: Srinagar Floating Vegetable Market
attractions.description: Each morning before 7 am, dozens of shikaras loaded with fresh vegetables grown on the Dal Lake's floating gardens converge near the Nehru Park shore for a floating wholesale market. Vendors pass produce hand to hand between boats in near-darkness, headlamps and lanterns lighting the transaction. It is entirely a local market, not a tourist attraction — which makes witnessing it all the more remarkable.
attractions.whyVisit: Watch the most extraordinary market in India from a shikara at dawn — a floating wholesale vegetable exchange unchanged in centuries.

attractions.name: Pari Mahal (Palace of Fairies)
attractions.description: A Mughal-era terraced garden and ruined palace complex perched on the southern spur of Zabarwan hill above Chashme Shahi, Pari Mahal was built in the mid-17th century by Dara Shikoh, elder son of Shah Jahan, as a library and astrological observatory. Six terraces of flower beds and water channels climb the hillside, and the illuminated ruins are visible from across Dal Lake on clear evenings.
attractions.whyVisit: An illuminated Mughal garden-palace ruin with the best evening view of Dal Lake in Srinagar.
attractions.bestTime: Late afternoon for views; after dark for illuminations

attractions.name: Jamia Masjid Rainawari
attractions.description: Less visited than the more famous Jama Masjid of Nowhatta, the mosque at Rainawari near the Dal Lake shore is a fine example of traditional Kashmiri wooden mosque architecture, with a distinctive tower built in the Kashmiri pagoda style. The neighbourhood around it retains the character of old Srinagar: narrow lanes, woodworkers' shops, and neighbourhood tea houses.
attractions.whyVisit: A beautiful neighbourhood mosque in old Kashmiri architectural style, surrounded by the authentic fabric of old Srinagar.

attractions.name: Khanqah Shah Hamadan Shikara Route
attractions.description: The full shikara circuit of Dal Lake takes in not just the Mughal gardens and Char Chinar but also the Jhelum River branch that runs through the old city, passing under the nine historic bridges connecting the old quarters. The view of Shah Hamadan Mosque from the river, with its elaborate wooden eaves and riverside ghats, is one of Srinagar's most historic urban waterfront scenes.
attractions.whyVisit: See Srinagar's historic waterfront — Shah Hamadan Mosque and the nine old Jhelum bridges — from the water.

attractions.name: Maharaja's Palace (Gulab Bhavan)
attractions.description: The summer palace of the Dogra rulers of Kashmir, perched on the ridge above Srinagar with commanding views of Dal Lake and the city, is now a heritage hotel managed by J&K Tourism. The Mughal-European hybrid architecture, formal gardens, and the durbar hall with its original furnishings make it a significant piece of Kashmiri royal history accessible to non-guests through the main gate during the day.
attractions.whyVisit: Tour the former summer palace of Kashmir's last Maharaja, a grand heritage building overlooking Dal Lake.

attractions.name: Indira Gandhi Memorial Tulip Garden
attractions.description: Asia's largest tulip garden covers 30 hectares on the Zabarwan hillside above Dal Lake and holds over 1.5 million tulip bulbs of more than 60 varieties. It blooms in a spectacular cascade of red, yellow, white, and purple during a narrow window each spring. The hillside terracing means every terrace offers a different floral view with Dal Lake and Srinagar city in the background.
attractions.whyVisit: Asia's largest tulip garden in full bloom against the backdrop of Dal Lake — a Kashmir spring spectacle.

attractions.name: Dastkar Artisan Market
attractions.description: Periodically organised under government and NGO patronage near Dal Lake, the Dastkar Kashmir bazaar brings together master craftspeople from across the valley — pashmina weavers, papier-mache artists, walnut woodcarvers, sozni embroiderers, and copperworkers. Unlike fixed shops, this setting allows direct conversation with the artisans and provides context for understanding the extraordinary skill behind each piece.
attractions.whyVisit: Buy authentic Kashmir handicrafts directly from master artisans — the most transparent and ethically sourced option in the city.

attractions.name: Wular Lake
attractions.description: Located 60 km northwest of Srinagar near Bandipora, Wular is the largest freshwater lake in South Asia and a Ramsar-designated wetland. The lake is critically important for migratory waterfowl and hosts tens of thousands of bar-headed geese, common teal, and pochards each autumn. The drive from Srinagar passes through the Sopore apple belt and the lake itself can be crossed by traditional wooden boats.
attractions.whyVisit: South Asia's largest freshwater lake and a world-class migratory bird habitat, an easy day trip from Srinagar.

attractions.name: Makhdoom Sahib Shrine
attractions.description: Perched high on the Hari Parbat hillside, the Makhdoom Sahib Dargah is the tomb of Sheikh Hamza Makhdoom, the patron saint of Kashmir, who lived from 1494 to 1576. The ascent up the steep lane through the old quarter of Hawal passes teahouses, bookshops, and neighbourhood mosques. The dargah terrace offers one of the finest elevated views of Dal Lake and the Zabarwan range.
attractions.whyVisit: Climb to the Sufi shrine of Kashmir's patron saint for a rooftop view of Dal Lake and old Srinagar.

attractions.name: Hari Parbat Fort
attractions.description: The hilltop fort overlooking Srinagar was built by Afghan Governor Atta Mohammed Khan in the 18th century on a hill sacred to Hindus as the abode of Goddess Sharika. The 18th-century ramparts enclose temples, a mosque, and a Sikh gurdwara — a rare multi-faith complex. The fort's battlements offer sweeping views of Dal Lake, the Jhelum Valley, and Srinagar's old quarters below.
attractions.whyVisit: An 18th-century hilltop fort enshrining Hindu, Muslim, and Sikh sacred sites with the finest aerial view of Srinagar.

attractions.name: Badamwari (Almond Garden)
attractions.description: Located at the foot of Hari Parbat hill, Badamwari (Almond Grove) is Srinagar's first harbinger of spring, with thousands of almond trees bursting into white and pale pink blossom each late February or March before most other trees have leafed. The garden hosts an almond blossom festival during peak bloom, attracting local families and photographers from across India.
attractions.whyVisit: Witness Srinagar's first spring — thousands of almond trees in blossom under Hari Parbat fort before the crowds arrive.

attractions.name: Cheeni Chowk Silver Bazaar
attractions.description: Hidden in the lanes of the old city near the Jama Masjid, the silver market of Cheeni Chowk is where Kashmiri silversmiths hammer, engrave, and sell traditional jewellery, salvers, and hookahs using techniques unchanged since the Mughal era. The delicate tracery work on silver and the oxidised finish on traditional Kashmiri ornaments are internationally recognised craft traditions.
attractions.whyVisit: Buy traditional Kashmiri silverwork directly from the craftsmen in the historic guild lanes of the old city.
attractions.bestTime: Morning when workshops are most active
